podcasts.name: Training Data
podcasts.title: Inside the Robot Data Factory: Mecka's Josh Gao on Sensorizing Humans to Train Robots
podcasts.description: Robotics never got the internet's gift of free training data, so someone has to manufacture it. Josh Gao, founder and CEO of Mecka AI, runs one of the largest robot data factories, and he explains what that actually involves: custom baseball caps and tactile gloves because nothing off the shelf captures force, 100-gigabit upload lines to move hundreds of petabytes, and custom quality gates. Josh lays out the training recipe the industry is converging on (roughly a million hours of egocentric human data, tens of thousands of hours of robot data, and a few hours of in-domain teleop ) and why tactile and simulation data still have to enter the "data pot of soup." He argues the field is still orders of magnitude behind Tesla's FSD, which spent a decade on two degrees of freedom while a robot hand has dozens. His take: there won't be a single GPT-3 moment for robotics, but a steady unlock of commercial tasks, starting with constrained industrial work and ending, he hopes, with robots mining asteroids. Hosted by Sonya Huang, Sequoia Capital 0:00 – Introduction 1:46 – What Mecka is: pixels, actions and logic 2:45 – Is robot data economically feasible without the internet? 4:15 – Teaching robots about carbon life 5:27 – Cloud kitchens, stablecoins and the path to robotics 7:03 – Entering robotics with a fresh lens 8:45 – What egocentric data is and why Mecka bet on it 10:09 – The first pilot: aunties and uncles with a mobile app 10:42 – Force data and tactile gloves 11:55 – Inside the operations of a data factory 14:41 – Heat-mapping the taxonomy of human work 15:42 – Quality gates, fraud and the McDonald’s POV videos 17:44 – Earning a margin as a data intermediary 19:33 – Millions of hours vs. Tesla’s decade 20:55 – Why it isn’t binary: unlocking commercial tasks along the way 22:02 – Home data is plentiful; home robots are the hardest 23:24 – Useful robots can be deployed today 24:35 – When robotics gets an FSD-style flywheel 26:42 – Deployment diffusion and the modern systems integrator 28:21 – Favorite vertical robot categories; mining an asteroid 30:08 – The hardware slate: Waymo-fying people 30:55 – EgoVerse 32:04 – The data pot of soup: the converged training mix 33:54 – Move 37 for robotics: AlphaGo and Federer 36:02 – World models and the training mix 36:58 – Will scaling the current mix get us to the promised land? 39:05 – Will the AGI labs steamroll robotics? 40:50 – Sci-fi roots and the Kawasaki Corleo 42:44 – How many robots in a decade?

podcasts.name: The Cognitive Revolution
podcasts.title: A World Model of Life: Biohub's Alex Rives on Virtual Cells, Measurement, & the $1.8B Data Push
podcasts.description: Alex Rives, Head of Science at Biohub and former lead of the ESM protein language model project, joins Nathan to discuss Biohub's mission to construct a predictive world model of life. Supported by an expanded $1.8 billion Virtual Biology Initiative alongside partners including the Department of Energy, NIH, Google DeepMind, and Meta, Rives outlines the massive push to map contextual cellular biology across hundreds of billions of cells. He breaks down why today's AI architectures fall short of simulating true virtual cells, emphasizing the need for breakthrough measurement technologies like the laser phase plate to observe biology at multi-scale resolution. The conversation examines the path toward achieving an information-level cell model within five years to ultimately transition medicine from traditional drugs to programmable interventions against cancer and degenerative disease. podcasts.title: #260 - Muse, Misalignment, Math
podcasts.description: Our 260th episode with a summary and discussion of last week's big AI news! Recorded on 10/07/2026 ; ok I lied, hopefully next ep will be out on time though... Hosted by Andrey Kurenkov and Jeremie Harris Feel free to email us your questions and feedback at andreyvkurenkov@gmail.com and/or hello@gladstone.ai Read out our text newsletter and comment on the podcast at https://lastweekin.ai/ In this episode: OpenAI began testing new visual ad formats in ChatGPT image generation, while TikTok launched an AI shopping assistant with one-click checkout, highlighting growing agent-mediated commerce and “generative engine optimization.” Meta’s Muse app hit 5M+ downloads with heavy in-house promotion, and Meta/Walmart/Stripe introduced a “personal agent protocol” to standardize how AI agents interact with businesses. ElevenLabs’ valuation reportedly doubled to $22B amid rising voice-agent demand, while major open releases included Reflection’s Beam (MoE, compute-efficient), Mistral’s 1T-parameter “Le Chunk” (Mistral Large 4), and Google’s Embedding Gemma 2 multimodal embedding model. Safety/policy and research updates included OpenAI misalignment reports, a resignation criticizing OpenAI’s culture and “iterative deployment,” California data-center regulation bills, dismissal of Google AI Overview antitrust suits, Meta’s new end-to-end software engineering benchmark, and OpenAI publishing 722 math manuscripts across 372 result families with potential cryptography and national security implications.
